name: PostgreSQL
description: Bounded PostgreSQL queries, transactions, row operations, schema discovery and database statistics using an embedded pure JavaScript pg client.

permissions.description: Connects over TCP/TLS to the configured PostgreSQL host with an encrypted password/CA secret or selected profile. Driver is embedded; no module installation. Filesystem and PGPASSWORD are conservatively declared because retained upstream fallback bytes reference them; emitted wrapper denies all fs API access, supplies empty PG environment, requires explicit password and accepts no credential/certificate file paths. Event ingress requires explicit administrator profiles, saved secret references and provider/relay setup. Installation never provisions subscriptions or executes trigger code.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Parameterized Query (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Parameterized Query. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Execute Statement (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Execute Statement. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Bounded Transaction (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Bounded Transaction. Executes 1–50 parameterized statements on one client, with COMMIT only after bounded results; ROLLBACK on failure where connected. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Explain Query (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Explain Query. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Select Rows (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Select Rows. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Insert Row (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Insert Row. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Upsert Row (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Upsert Row. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Update Matching Rows (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Update Matching Rows. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Delete Matching Rows (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Delete Matching Rows. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Connection Health (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Connection Health. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

Server Information. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL List Schemas (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
List Schemas. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL List Tables (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
List Tables. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL List Views (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
List Views. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL List Columns (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
List Columns. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL List Indexes (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
List Indexes. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL List Constraints (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
List Constraints. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL List Sequences (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
List Sequences. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL List Routines (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
List Routines. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL List Databases (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
List Databases. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL List Extensions (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
List Extensions. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Table Statistics (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Table Statistics. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Database Statistics (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Database Statistics. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Table Size (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Table Size. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Database Size (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Database Size. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Session Activity (Direct)
definitions.documentation:
Session Activity. Opens one connection and closes it in finally. Read operations use a READ ONLY transaction; database privileges remain authoritative. Mutations require request.confirm=true and $retries=0. Results retain ordered fields and array-valued rows so duplicate column names are preserved. Default result bounds: 1000 rows, 1 MiB; maximum 10000 rows, 1 MiB. One total 15s deadline by default (maximum 60s), server statement/lock/idle transaction timeouts, extended single-statement protocol. SQL/params are never interpolated; row operation identifiers are quoted. Do not retry uncertain mutations. Embeds audited pg 8.23.1 with complete third-party notices; no external driver install. Only explicit Node builtins are imported, process.env is empty inside the driver and fs APIs are denied. Filesystem permission is conservatively declared for retained fallback bytes. TLS verifies certificates by default. Use passwordSecret (default name POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD when configured) or a selected profile password. No long-lived listener, COPY, replication stream, migration runner or pool is provided. Sources: https://node-postgres.com/features/queries https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions https://node-postgres.com/apis/client https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-transaction.html

Semantic authoring: new logical ID with direct typed wrapper fields. Prior operation remains compatible. Absence/null/falsy, confirmations and provider behavior are preserved; typed result outputs remain alongside direct fields. No extra provider call.

definitions.name: PostgreSQL Notification Received (Relay) Event
definitions.description: Typed event emitted by PostgreSQL Notification Received (Relay).
definitions.documentation: Event output contract for PostgreSQL Notification Received (Relay). This trigger accepts the canonical version-1 postgresql envelope only; it does not authenticate or decode native provider requests. Required exact provider verification: Deploy a separately managed authenticated TLS PostgreSQL LISTEN client restricted to the intended database/channels. Do not install SQL triggers or alter the database automatically. Mapping: Emit notification.received for each delivered channel, payload and backend PID. Relay must assign a durable stable delivery ID before HTTP delivery; accountId identifies the authorized database. occurredAt is relay observation time because NOTIFY has no event timestamp. Canonical eventType values: notification.received. Required envelope: version=1, provider=postgresql, deliveryId, eventType, occurredAt (UTC ISO milliseconds), accountId, resource as the typed output schema. Omit no required fields; use explicit null where allowed. Filters accountId/resourceId are exact matches; blank disables a filter. At most 100 account+delivery IDs within 96 KiB deduplicate retries per group; state commits on trigger success before downstream completion. LISTEN/NOTIFY is transient; disconnected listeners miss events, and duplicate notifications within one transaction may be folded. This is an application notification, not automatic row-level CDC or a durable replication slot. Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-listen.html https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-notify.html

ingressRequirements.name: PostgreSQL notification relay
ingressRequirements.description: Manual prerequisite: separately maintained exact provider authentication/normalization relay. This release only accepts header-authenticated canonical envelopes from that relay.
setupSteps: Install this reviewed package release; no relay or subscription is installed.
Deploy an independently maintained provider-aware relay which implements the exact provider signature, challenge, authorization and replay rules described below.
Deploy a separately managed authenticated TLS PostgreSQL LISTEN client restricted to the intended database/channels. Do not install SQL triggers or alter the database automatically.

Emit notification.received for each delivered channel, payload and backend PID. Relay must assign a durable stable delivery ID before HTTP delivery; accountId identifies the authorized database. occurredAt is relay observation time because NOTIFY has no event timestamp.

Implement the exact canonical version-1 envelope and typed resource schemas documented by each selected trigger; forward one event per POST. Normalize account identity from the authorized provider connection, never from an untrusted request.

Persist one stable delivery ID per logical event across relay retries. Fanout IDs must include distinct native entity/event/status identity (or a persisted record ID); reusing a batch delivery ID or message ID across different statuses drops events. Authorize account/resources; bound payloads to 64 KiB and limit rate.
Save a separate relay-to-ONF callback secret; create a header-authenticated ingress profile for this requirement.
Bind the intended trigger node, configure the relay with its HTTPS callback URL, then deliberately enable workflow and entry.
Review relay limits, delivery identifiers, retries and downstream idempotency; test explicitly before production use.

Select saved node entry mode webhook explicitly; package metadata does not infer it. Create/select a profile for this exact installed requirement (installation.id + "/verified-events"), bind node.trigger.ingress.profileId, save the graph and deliberately enable workflow and entry only when setup is complete.
